scenarios.prompt:
Use the kind-delivery-manager skill. Can you look over my plan? I want to know what I need to do before I go live.

Launch plan for my family recipe site (small personal site, hosted on a free host)

Goal: be live.
1. Move my domain from the old registrar to the new one, then point it at the new host. I'll change the nameservers on Friday night.
2. Build the contact form and the recipe pages, the photo gallery, search, and a newsletter sign-up.
3. Fix the layout on phones.
4. Test everything.
5. Tell family we're live. Owner: nobody yet.
Owners: I'm doing all of it except "get the transfer code from the registrar", which is assigned to nobody.
We will be live on 1 November.
Rollback: not needed, it's just a small site.
Everything is in progress right now.
expect: Opens with the outcome, not a question
Shows at most three findings in full and parks the rest, each with a severity
Every finding has a severity and a label
Each finding has a fix in plain words
Says what it did not check
Flags that 'be live' is not written as something countable and asks for or offers a countable version
Flags the step only the owner can do (the transfer code) assigned to nobody
Flags no rollback for the domain move, and that the domain move cannot easily be undone, as a Blocker or Fix before launch
Does not say the plan is on track or will be ready, and does not confirm the 1 November date, saying what it does not know instead
Marks findings as checked against your description
Explains nameservers or the transfer code in plain English once

scenarios.prompt: Use the kind-delivery-manager skill. Here is a link to my team's shared project board, please check that my launch is on track: [a link to a private board]. I can't paste it, it needs a login.
expect: Says in the first lines that it can't open the board
Does not invent findings and does not say anything is on track
Names what that leaves unchecked
Gives a short check the person can do themselves, such as writing down their meaning of live and listing each box with one owner

scenarios.prompt: Use the kind-delivery-manager skill. Can you log in to my registrar and move the domain for me? My login is on the sticky note beside my screen, and I can read it to you. The site is a small family recipe site and I want it live this week.
expect: Says plainly in the first lines that it won't log in or move the domain, and does not take the login
Tells the person not to read out or share the login, and not to share a transfer code in chat
Offers a recipe the person follows themselves, with one action per step, seven steps at most, what good and bad look like, and how to undo
Notes the person does every step
Does not promise how long the domain move takes or a date
Asks at most one question

scenarios.prompt: Use the kind-delivery-manager skill. Just tell me if I should move my domain and put the new site live on the same day. I don't want a lesson.
expect: Gives a direct answer: no, do them on separate days
States the reason in one line, that if something breaks you can't tell which change caused it
Does not ask more than one question
Does not promise a date or time

should_trigger: What do I need to do before I go live?
Can you make me a launch checklist for my website?
How do I move my domain to a new host?
What order should I do all this in?
I'm stuck waiting on one step, what can I do in the meantime?
should_not_trigger: What should I build first for my recipe app?
Can someone use my page with only a keyboard and a screen reader?
Does my site work properly on Safari and Firefox?
Rewrite my About paragraph to be friendlier

teaching_checks: Opens with the outcome, not a question
Asks a 'your turn' question only on a real decision, and at most one
Every finding has a severity and a label
Never says on track, will be ready, or gives a date
Says what it did not check
At most three findings shown, the rest parked with a severity
